name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,317

entries.clue: Whimsically extinguish pleasure? (7)

blocks.note: read playfully: DE- as in defrost, attached to a word for illumination
a plain synonym for great enjoyment

annotation.surface: Someone asks, half joking, whether snuffing things out could count as fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whimsically' warns that the first definition is a made-up word: DE- as in de-ice or defrost, applied to LIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure, and as a verb or noun it swaps cleanly for it.

entries.clue: Contract to tidy up parlour (7,4)

blocks.note: to draw in = to contract, pull inwards
to groom = to tidy up one's appearance

annotation.surface: A cleaner is hired to spruce up the front room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a job agreement; it is the verb, to shrink or draw in. The split DRAW IN + GROOM runs across the word break.
annotation.definitionFit: A parlour is a sitting room for receiving guests, which is what a drawing room is.

entries.clue: WC Fields’ conclusion on cathedral city, more or less (7)

indicatorNotes.conclusion: the end of 'Fields' is its last letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, 'on' puts the next piece after, stacked below

blocks.note: Ely, the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

annotation.surface: The comedian W.C. Fields passes a vague verdict on some cathedral city.
annotation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields was an American comic actor; split apart, his initials are a toilet. Ely is a small English cathedral city near Cambridge, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: Loosely means roughly, not exactly: 'loosely translated' is 'more or less translated'.

entries.clue: Gran opted to change into responsible adult (9)

indicatorNotes.to change: the letters of GRAN OPTED change into a new order

annotation.surface: Grandmother decides it is time to grow up and act her age.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes Gran the one changing; in fact her letters are what change. A grandmother is a natural candidate to be a godparent, which helps the disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: A godparent is an adult who takes on responsibility for a child's upbringing, especially its religious guidance.

entries.clue: Some idiot ran ceremony in stupor (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

annotation.surface: A dazed fool somehow ended up officiating at a ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles three words, starting on the last letter of 'idiot'.
annotation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed, half-conscious state, as is a stupor.

entries.clue: Make gentle flapping motion with a newspaper? (4)

blocks.note: w = with, the standard abbreviation (as in w/)

annotation.surface: Fanning yourself with a folded newspaper on a hot day.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads the whole clue as one action; only 'Make gentle flapping motion' is the definition. The Financial Times is a London business paper, familiar to setters as FT.
annotation.definitionFit: To waft is to move something gently through the air, as with a fan.

entries.clue: Comedian’s salary cut (3)

indicatorNotes.cut: the salary is cut short, losing its last letter

annotation.surface: A comic's pay has been slashed.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as a possessive; it stands for 'is', joining the comedian to what he is made from.
annotation.definitionFit: A wag is a joker, someone always making witty remarks.

entries.clue: Tripped over a guy (5)

blocks.note: to trip over is to fall; fell is its past tense

annotation.surface: Someone stumbled over a man lying in the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tripped over a guy' suggests tripping over something; 'over' belongs with 'Tripped', and 'a' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Fella is informal for fellow, a man or guy.

entries.clue: Stay away from American invalid (5)

blocks.note: invalid as an adjective: empty, of no legal force

annotation.surface: Advice to keep clear of an ailing American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' tempts as the noun, a sick person; it is the adjective, not valid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: steering clear of a person or place is exactly what the answer means.

entries.clue: Surprisingly genial, Charlie is adorable (7)

indicatorNotes.Surprisingly: GENIAL comes out in a surprising new order

blocks.note: Charlie = C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Charlie, it turns out, is friendly and delightful.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a person in the scene; he is only the letter C.
annotation.definitionFit: Angelic, like an angel, is used of a sweet, adorable child.

entries.clue: Make clear: less clarity is bad (11)

indicatorNotes.bad: the letters are in a bad, disordered state

annotation.surface: A writing tip: be clear, because muddiness is a fault.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a neat piece of advice, with 'clarity' in it pointing straight at the definition's meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Used figuratively of ideas or plans taking definite form, as a solution forms sharp-edged crystals.

entries.clue: Cold water lovely when face is scratched (3)

indicatorNotes.when face is scratched: the face, the front letter, is scratched out

blocks.note: NICE loses its first letter N

annotation.surface: A swim in cold water is lovely, except when you graze your face.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face' is the first letter here, not a person's face.
annotation.definitionFit: Ice is water at its coldest, frozen solid.

entries.clue: Current business partner (9)

annotation.surface: Someone introduces the person they now run a firm with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Partner' reads as a noun, a business partner; it is the verb, to go along with someone.
annotation.definitionFit: To partner someone at a dance or dinner is to accompany them.

entries.clue: When email is rewritten? In the interval (9)

indicatorNotes.rewritten: the letters are written out again in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone asks what happens in the gap while an email is being redrafted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When' looks like a joining word, but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Meanwhile means in the intervening time, in the interval.

entries.clue: Reported crafty bloke in natural water feature (6)

indicatorNotes.Reported: the word is passed on by speech, so it is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a geezer is British slang for a man, often a streetwise, crafty one

annotation.surface: News of a cunning fellow spotted in a garden fountain.
annotation.walkthrough: In British speech GEYSER is said 'geezer', and a geezer is slang for a bloke, often a shifty one. North Americans say 'guy-zer', so the pun works best in a British accent.
annotation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that shoots water into the air, a water feature made by nature.

entries.clue: Incentive from coach to become corrupt (6)

blocks.note: a coach is a railway carriage, or car
to rot is to decay, to become corrupt

annotation.surface: A sports coach offers a bribe that leads a player astray.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a trainer; here it is a railway carriage, a car.
annotation.definitionFit: A carrot is an incentive, from the carrot dangled in front of a donkey.

entries.clue: Group of soldiers shortened course of treatment (7)

indicatorNotes.shortened: the word is made shorter by losing its last letter

blocks.note: REGIMENT without its last letter T

annotation.surface: A military unit cut short its programme of medical care.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'shortened' a verb acting on the course; it acts on the soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or medical treatment.

entries.clue: Very sad, finally got something to smoke served up (6)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down clue, 'up' turns the word to read from the bottom

annotation.surface: A sorry figure who at last got his smoke brought to him.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the definition from the wordplay; 'Very sad' is the definition, not a comment on the smoker.
annotation.definitionFit: Tragic means deeply sad or distressing.

entries.clue: Six deliveries in cricket somehow worth extra run (9)

indicatorNotes.somehow: WORTH turns into THROW somehow, by rearranging

blocks.note: an over is six balls bowled

annotation.surface: A cricket over that somehow yields a bonus run.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls from one bowler, and an overthrow is a fielder's throw that misses the stumps, letting the batters run again.
annotation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is an extra run scored from a wild throw by a fielder.

entries.clue: Surpass 40 in Rome, it’s said (5)

indicatorNotes.it’s said: the letters are spoken, so we hear them

blocks.note: 40 is XL in Roman numerals; say 'ex-el'

annotation.surface: Someone claims you can outdo forty others in Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' points to Roman numerals: X is 10, L is 50, so XL is 40.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to outdo or rise above others.

entries.clue: Turning on setter (3)

indicatorNotes.Turning: the word is turned around to read backwards

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is the leg side

annotation.surface: A crossword setter is switched on, or turned against.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle's author; it is hair gel, which sets hair. 'On' as LEG is cricket: the on side of the field is also called the leg side.
annotation.definitionFit: Gel is a styling product that sets hair in place, a setter.

entries.clue: Making fun of second Conservative leader (7)

blocks.note: mo = a moment, a second ("wait a mo")

annotation.surface: Someone is ridiculing the Tory deputy leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second Conservative leader' reads as a deputy or the next party chief; each word is its own piece. Mo is British slang for a moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe ridiculing someone, teasing them with scorn.

entries.clue: Mischievous child of one politician (3)

annotation.surface: A politician's naughty kid.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the child belong to a politician; 'of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An imp is a mischievous child, from the little devil of folklore.

entries.clue: Setter’s mostly tender feet (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word is used, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: the setter speaks of himself as I, so 'setter is' = I AM
tender = bid, an offer; BID without its last letter

annotation.surface: The crossword setter admits to having rather sore feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tender' suggests sore; it is the noun, a bid or offer, as in a public tender. 'Feet' are metrical feet in poetry.
annotation.definitionFit: Iambi, plural of iambus, are metrical feet of one short syllable then one long, as in 'today'.

entries.clue: Collapse of pound welcomed by dandy (4)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: the pound is taken in by the dandy, placed inside him

blocks.note: a fop is a vain, overdressed man

annotation.surface: A fashionable gent is delighted as sterling crashes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a currency crash; 'Collapse' is the definition and 'of' just joins it to the wordplay. L for pound comes from the Latin libra, as in the £ sign.
annotation.definitionFit: To flop is to collapse, as into a chair; a flop is also a collapse or failure.

entries.clue: Disinfect tips in outskirts of Carlisle (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the tips go inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.outskirts: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of CARLISLE
to tip is to lean over

annotation.surface: Rubbish tips on the edge of Carlisle need a thorough cleaning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tips' reads as rubbish dumps, apt for disinfecting; it is the verb, to lean. Carlisle is a city in northern England. LEANS goes inside C...E.
annotation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make thoroughly clean, which is what disinfecting does.
